# Uploaded Bhavsadhan house tables

The seven supplied `Raphel*Placidus_User_ST_*.xlsx` workbooks uploaded on 12 October 2026 are retained unchanged in `source/` and are the active automatic source. They supply tropical Placidus cusps for 61 whole northern latitudes, 0° through 60°, and sidereal time from 00:00:00 through 24:00:00. The earlier Swiss workbooks remain in that folder for reference and are not combined with the active Raphael sheets. The new printed values match the previous printed columns. No claim is made that these files are an independently verified transcription of a historical Raphael book.

`import_tables.py` accepts the new seven-column layout: **ST HH:MM:SS, 10H, 11H, 12H, Asc DM, 2H, 3H**. It validates sheet names, the complete actual ST clock, sign/degree/minute values, ordering and matching midnight endpoints. It removes 671 identical boundary repeats, retaining 22,021 unique latitude/time rows. `tables.json` records filenames, SHA-256 hashes and source precision. Whole-degree houses are read with their signs; Asc DM is degrees + minutes/60. The `values` API array is now the numeric conversion of these same printed values; the new uploads contain no additional precise numeric columns. The importer prefers all seven Raphel workbooks, falling back to the older Swiss layout only if no Raphel files are present. Run `python vendor/houses/import_tables.py` with openpyxl to rebuild the packed data.

The standalone HTML embeds this data and both calculation modules, so tables work offline and in the private calculation worker without fetching files. Source XLSX files are not required at runtime.

Automatic Bhavsadhan interpolates circular ecliptic longitude first between actual tabulated sidereal times, then between the two adjacent integer latitudes. The table has unequal time intervals; it does not assume a four-minute grid. Exact grid inputs retain the selected source-column values, including their printed degree/minute precision. At 360° and midnight, interpolation follows the short angular interval instead of averaging 359° and 0° across the zodiac. Six opposite cusps are derived at +180°. The selected annual KP DMS anchors are interpolated at the actual birth UTC instant, including calendar-year/leap-year boundaries. KP ayanamsha is subtracted once; rounding happens only when writing final cusp fields to one arcsecond. An explicitly selected manual ayanamsha remains available in the unlocked administrator worksheet. Unlike manual legacy arithmetic, automatic interpolation does not round the correction to whole arcminutes.

For a native birth chart using Automatic ST, the software advances the selected ephemeris ST reference by the actual sidereal rotation from its reference UTC instant to the birth UTC instant. It then replaces the standard meridian with the native longitude once. The supplied adjusted ephemeris's ST +1 second is preserved, not added a second time. Time zone, DST and date rollover come from the native instant. Full precision reaches the lookup; `birthPlaceSiderealTime` displays the rounded final time. This avoids the earlier multi-second drift caused by rounding intermediate legacy LMT/10:6 corrections. Explicit manual ST still uses the entered `birthPlaceSiderealTime`. Instant Prashna uses local apparent sidereal time at the exact entered UTC instant and longitude. Numbered KP Horary retains its existing exact numbered Ascendant and date-specific solver. The source workbooks have no dated obliquity metadata: this mode deliberately interpolates their reference values rather than claiming date-specific accuracy.

The compact source selector lives in **ADM → Raphael houses**. Uploaded tables are the default. Southern latitudes or latitudes above 60° use the existing date-specific Placidus solver at the same local sidereal orientation; source status identifies that fallback. No extrapolation or north/south mirroring is performed. Polar-circle locations remain unsupported and clear calculated cusp results. **Date-specific Placidus** explicitly uses that solver throughout. **Manual table entry** preserves the existing editable worksheet method. Editing a source cusp/time bracket switches to Manual. Ordinary saved-chart imports refresh automatic sources and dates. Explicit manual source work is preserved while the administrator panel is unlocked; new saves retain the selected source.

Changing birth details or pressing the ordinary Calculate button refreshes the cusp worksheet, kundali, significators and dependent reports automatically. No separate table-import or house-calculation button is needed.

The private customer worker always restores automatic house/ephemeris sources and annual KP ayanamsha on calculation or chart import. Customer exports omit these administrator worksheet settings; importing such an export does not fall back to stale manual worksheet values.

Validation: `PYTHONPATH=tests python -m unittest test_house_tables test_automatic_calculations -v`. Checks cover all source rows/hashes, all exact latitude/ST grid entries, interpolation, wrapping, Meeus-independent sidereal progression, birth-instant annual ayanamsha, midnight/DST/leap-year cases, offline use, the private worker and saved-chart repeatability.

The main source rows show the actual lower-latitude Excel entries: whole degrees only for houses X, XI, XII, II and III, and degrees:minutes for the Ascendant. A compact collapsed section shows the adjacent upper-latitude Excel rows in those same units when needed. Fractional latitude blends are not written into the source fields. The derived smaller-ST and difference rows are explicitly labelled as latitude-interpolated and use D:M:S; final cusps retain the full-precision circular interpolation and are rounded once to D:M:S. This source-display change does not round or alter the cusp calculation. The printed inputs have the precision supplied in the Excel sheets; no unprinted seconds are invented.

DMS is the calculated display resolution, not proof of arcsecond source accuracy. The new sheets round X/XI/XII/II/III to whole degrees and Ascendant to whole minutes. Interpolation cannot recover omitted source precision. The existing Date-specific Placidus mode can be selected in ADM when date-specific astronomical cusps are required.
